newsitem.title: UK: LME copper eases towards $2,000 in late trading.
newsitem.headline: LME copper eases towards $2,000 in late trading.

text.p: LME copper edged lower, hovering above the $2,000 level in late inter-office trading on Monday evening after earlier failing on the upside.
Three months copper was indicated at $2,003/06 per tonne at 1900 GMT after a kerb close of $2,016 and a high of $2,042.
Although another stocks draw was expected on Tuesday, some analysts were wondering how long inventories could keep declining.

"Having seen 129,950 tonnes drawn down out of LME warehouses since the beginning of September, it is now likely that the Chinese requirements have been met, so the rate of stock drawdown may now fall," said analyst William Adams of broker Rudolf Wolff in a report.
Most of the other metals were a touch softer, with nickel slipping under the $7,400 level. It was indicated at $7,370/80 after a kerb close of $7,409.
